title: Guideline-Based Medical Reasoning in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2512.03838v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) excel at medical question-answering, yet progress toward medical reasoning models is limited by the lack of scalable, trustworthy reasoning supervision. We propose tapping into the so far underused resource of medical consensus guidelines. These map numerical clinical measurements to disease scores and can optionally be curated for site-specific exceptions. Automatically generating gold-standard reasoning chains from consensus rules enables both large-scale supervised fine-tuning and automatic evaluation. Applying SOFA, SAPS-II, and Sepsis-3 guidelines to MIMIC-III, we show that small fine-tuned models significantly outperform larger one-shot prompted models in derivation correctness and F1 score, achieving near-perfect deductive inference and reliable exception handling. Trustworthy step-by-step reasoning does not reliably emerge from one-shot prompting, even when models receive the consensus definition

translated_title: 基于指南的大语言模型医学推理
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在医学问答方面表现出色，但医学推理模型的发展受到缺乏可扩展、可信赖的推理监督的限制。我们提出利用迄今为止未被充分开发的资源——医学共识指南。这些指南将数值化的临床测量指标映射到疾病评分，并可选择性地针对特定机构的例外情况进行定制。从共识规则中自动生成黄金标准推理链，既能支持大规模监督微调，也能支持自动评估。我们将SOFA、SAPS-II和Sepsis-3指南应用于MIMIC-III数据集，结果显示经过微调的小模型在推导正确性和F1分数上显著优于更大的单次提示模型，实现了接近完美的演绎推理和可靠的例外情况处理。即使在模型获得共识定义的情况下，可信赖的逐步推理也无法通过单次提示可靠地产生。
tldr: 该论文提出从医学共识指南（如SOFA、SAPS-II和Sepsis-3）自动生成黄金标准推理链作为监督信号，证明经过微调的小模型在医学推理任务上显著优于更大的单次提示模型，且单次提示无法可靠地产生可信赖的逐步推理。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes automatically generating gold-standard reasoning chains from medical consensus guidelines (SOFA, SAPS-II, Sepsis-3) as supervision, demonstrating that small fine-tuned models significantly outperform larger one-shot prompted models in medical reasoning, while trustworthy step-by-step reasoning does not reliably emerge from one-shot prompting.
